context: Pick ONE of: (a) make ledger export opt-in per adapter until each records its settings, so an uninstrumented adapter publishes no claim rather than a false noop; or (b) instrument datafusion-df and dask-df _apply_tuning() with _record_runtime_tuning() before the export call. Option (b) is the fuller fix; option (a) is the safer interim. Decide explicitly and record the rationale in the PR body.
description:
chatgpt-codex-connector review finding on merged PR #1269 (P2, benchbox/platforms/dataframe/tuning_mixin.py:284). Deferred from the PR-review sweep in PR #1292 because the fix is a design fork that determines what validation_status published runs carry; tracked in GitHub issue #1293.

The ledger writer now runs for EVERY TuningConfigurableMixin adapter, but production adapters whose _apply_tuning() was never instrumented (notably datafusion-df and dask-df) export a status derived from an empty ledger. For example DataFusion's thread_count changes _target_partitions but adds no _record_runtime_tuning() entry, so set_tuning_info() publishes validation_status="noop" and no applied hash for a run that was genuinely tuned.
Thread: https://github.com/joeharris76/BenchBox/pull/1269#discussion_r3634087174

anti_patterns.dont: leave the export path emitting noop for an adapter that was actually tuned
anti_patterns.instead: either record the real settings or publish no claim at all
anti_patterns.why: a false noop is published evidence that the run was untuned

preserves.behavior: An untuned DataFrame run still reports noop legitimately
Instrumented adapters (polars-df and any other already recording entries) keep their current validation_status and applied hash
